description: Machine-readable source of truth for EngineOS risk, autonomy, gates, parallelism, retry, router escalation, repair-loop, circuit-breaker and telemetry policy — eleven blocks (risk, autonomy, gates, parallelism, retry, prompt_signals, router, repair, breaker, hitl, telemetry), added across P1 (risk/autonomy/gates/parallelism/retry) through P7 (telemetry). rules/risk-autonomy.md, rules/gates.md and rules/parallelism.md stay the human-readable mirror and are not edited to match. scripts/validate-engineos.sh checks this file: C16 extracts prose numbers (wave cap, retry attempts/escalations, spec threshold) and enum tables and compares them against this file; C17 checks prompt_signals; C18 checks the router block; C20 checks repair; C22 checks telemetry; C24 checks parallelism.backpressure (the dispatch loop's admission control, answered by kernel.sh admit and mirrored in rules/parallelism.md 'Backpressure'); C25 checks breaker (the per-resource circuit breaker, answered by kernel.sh breaker and mirrored in rules/parallelism.md 'Circuit breaker'); C26 checks hitl (human-in-the-loop as a queryable entity, answered by kernel.sh hitl, folded into resolve-task as .hitl, and mirrored in rules/risk-autonomy.md 'Human-in-the-loop'); C27 checks telemetry.exec_journal (the agent-span journal, written by the hooks through hooks/lib-common.sh's hook_span and mirrored in rules/observability.md 'Agent traces'), C28 the retrieval-metrics reference and its RAG mirror, and C29 the adoption entrypoint wiring — so a future prose edit or block change that diverges fails CI.

inputs.low: Trivially undone, e.g. a git revert.
inputs.high: Irreversible, or reversible only with data loss.
Production, other teams, or external consumers.
PII, credentials, financial, or clinical data.
Public/published API, DB schema, or event payload.

levels.permitted: Recommend, draft, or propose a diff — do not apply it.
Apply reversible changes in the working tree.
Apply, but a human gate precedes any external effect.
Bounded autonomous operation, monitored, with a kill switch.

backpressure.note: Admission control for the orchestrator's dispatch loop. Capacity is wave_concurrency_cap above (never a second copy). Answered by scripts/kernel.sh admit; mirrored in rules/parallelism.md 'Backpressure'. defer = hold the unit for the next wave; reject = stop planning, report BLOCKED, re-plan with a human (a hitl reason).

rows.reason: cap {cap} reached; {queued} of {max_queued_units} queued — hold the unit for the next wave
cap {cap} reached and queue full ({queued}/{max_queued_units}) — stop planning, report BLOCKED, re-plan with a human (hitl: budget-exhausted)

prompt_signals.note: Prompt-classification EREs for kernel.sh scale (were hardcoded in the UserPromptSubmit advisor before the kernel owned them). Countable nouns in scale are plural-only on purpose: 'add a component' is one unit and must not trip fan-out advice. design_weak only counts alongside an action verb.

repair.note: Check-level failure policy: what to do when a validation check is red during a fix loop. The agent-unit counterpart is the retry block; both encode the same bound discipline (rules/parallelism.md: two attempts, one escalation, then a human) over different failure kinds — an agent unit reports an envelope status, a check exits nonzero. Read by scripts/kernel.sh repair; hooks/stop-verify.sh reads the numbers for its block message. The numeric agreement with retry is evidence-based, not law: if P7 telemetry ever justifies a different check bound, this block changes and nothing else does.

by_situation.reason: the check could not run — that is a tooling gap, not a code defect; report it, consume no fix attempt (hooks/stop-verify.sh: never block on infra quirks)
green on re-run with no diff is a broken test, not a pass — fix or delete within the week, never retry-until-green (rules/testing.md)

never_repair_answer.reason: situation {situation} is on the never-repair list — a fix that weakens the check or changes behavior is not a fix; escalate to a human on the first occurrence

ladder.reason: first red — fix and re-run the check at the same tier
the same check failed twice — escalate one model tier for the fix and re-run once; that is the last attempt (rules/models.md)
the bound is exhausted — stop, report the check red with what was tried; a loop continued past this point is sampling until it looks right, not fixing (rules/parallelism.md)

infra_patterns.pattern: cannot find (project|target) |does not have (a|an) .* target|cannot find configuration for task
missing script:|command "<t>" not found|find a script named "<t>"
No module named (ruff|pyright|pytest)|command not found|No such file or directory: .*(ruff|pyright|pytest)

breaker.note: Resource-level failure policy — the third failure block, and deliberately not a variant of the other two. retry asks "try this UNIT again?" and counts attempts against an agent envelope status; repair asks "fix this CHECK again?" and counts attempts against a nonzero exit; breaker asks "why are we still calling this RESOURCE?" — one of the scopes below: provider, mcp, tool or agent — and counts consecutive failures against the resource itself. Folding it into retry would tie a per-unit attempt counter to a per-resource health signal, so every fresh unit would rediscover a dead dependency from attempt one. Consult breaker BEFORE retry. Read by scripts/kernel.sh breaker, which is the transition table and nothing more: the orchestrator owns the state and the consecutive-failure count, taken from the exec journal (span_kind tool or model, status FAILED, same tool/provider). scopes is advisory: it is the orchestrator's vocabulary for keying a breaker's state per resource, and no kernel code path reads it, so C25a's non-empty check and C25c's prose grep are the only things holding those ids to the frozen contract. Mirrored in rules/parallelism.md 'Circuit breaker'; scripts/validate-engineos.sh C25 checks the block, the kernel's transitions and the prose together. ADR: docs/adr/2026-09-03-circuit-breaker-separate-from-retry.md.

transitions.reason: {failures} consecutive failures reached threshold {failure_threshold} — stop calling this resource for {cooldown_waves} wave(s); route around or report DEGRADED
cooldown elapsed — allow {half_open_probes} probe call(s); no fan-out through this resource until it closes
cooldown not elapsed — do not call; route around or report DEGRADED
probe succeeded — resource recovered; reset the failure count to 0
probe failed — reopen for another cooldown

hitl.note: Human-in-the-loop as a queryable entity rather than a tier's implication. autonomy.ceiling_by_risk says how far a unit may go alone; this block says when a HUMAN must decide and names WHY, so the decision is auditable instead of inferred. Answered by scripts/kernel.sh hitl, folded into resolve-task as .hitl from a CLASSIFIED tier only (decision_rules.any_high) and never from a risk floor, because a floor is an input to classification and a gate announced off one is gate theatre (rules/gates.md); on a floor-only prompt .hitl is null and hooks/prompt-advisor.sh turns task_contract.risk_floor into an instruction to classify rather than a gate, announced by hooks/prompt-advisor.sh, mirrored in rules/risk-autonomy.md 'Human-in-the-loop'; C26 checks the block, the kernel's answers and the prose together. reasons is the CLOSED vocabulary a gate may cite — a gate citing anything else produces a record no one can argue with, which is the hole this block exists to close; the list order is the kernel's emission order. situations is what --situation accepts ON TOP OF retry.never_retry (whose ids all collapse to the single reason never-retry-situation), and the two lists are disjoint so the union lookup stays unambiguous. budget-exhausted is deliberately in BOTH reasons and situations: it is a reason a human is needed AND a situation a caller reports, and kernel.sh admit's reject message embeds the literal 'hitl: budget-exhausted' — C26d couples that literal to this list and to the kernel's own --situation reject answer so the three cannot drift apart. autonomy_after is a DROP and never a raise: one level below the ceiling passed in, no lower than A1, capped at risk high by autonomy.high_with_thin_evidence, and never above the level given -- so A0 stays A0. record_home is where the decision gets written down; a tier that required a human and carries no such record has not passed its gate. ADR: docs/adr/2026-09-03-hitl-as-kernel-entity.md.

telemetry.note: Kernel-decision event capture: which routes, decision rules and verifications actually fired, as ids and outcomes only — never prompt text (value_pattern has no whitespace class; scripts/telemetry.sh rejects on append and validate). Written by hooks/prompt-advisor.sh and hooks/stop-verify.sh to $GITDIR/engineos-telemetry/<session_id>.jsonl in the consumer project, only where .engineos/ exists (the scaffolder's own opt-in gate) and ENGINEOS_TELEMETRY is not 0. Read by skills/retro (step 1) and scripts/usage-report.sh; reaped by hooks/ensure-project-layout.sh after retention_days. Events live in .git and never reach CI — validate-engineos.sh C22 checks this policy and the plumbing, never the data. written_by is an array because one event can have several writers, which supersedes the one-writer-per-event shape recorded in docs/specs/2026-08-06-decision-kernel-p7-telemetry.md. The samples are asserted by C22b against the running telemetry.sh, the self-validating-registry pattern of routing.json's sample_path and router.fixtures. Attempt-level repair/retry outcomes are deliberately absent: no hook mediates those model-invoked kernel calls, and their designed home is the exec-journal schema, written by the ai-se-os runner follow-on.

exec_journal.note: Agent-span capture: what actually HAPPENED when agents ran, as the counterpart to the events above, which record what EngineOS DECIDED. One session is one trace (trace_id = session_id) and every dispatched agent, router decision and verification gate is a span in it; span_kinds is the closed vocabulary, mirrored in scripts/exec-journal.sh's VALID_SPAN_KINDS constant and compared against it by validate-engineos.sh C27a, so the two cannot be renamed apart. The schema is scripts/exec-journal.sh, whose v2 span fields are all OPTIONAL: a v1 line carries none of the keys and stays valid, and backward compatibility is the contract. Containment, stated the same way here, in scripts/exec-journal.sh's header and in rules/observability.md 'Agent traces': every field EXCEPT note is a slug matching the same telemetry.value_pattern above, and the validator rejects a line where one of them is not; note is the only field that admits FREE TEXT, but it is NOT the only field carrying attacker-influenced content and a consumer must not treat it as the single untrusted field: a harness-supplied value transits dash-joined through hook_slug, so its characters still reach disk, and the value_pattern slug class admits '.' and '/' -- '../../../../etc/cron.d/x' is a valid slug that exec-journal.sh validate passes clean. A journal field is therefore NEVER safe as a filesystem path component; a consumer building a path from one narrows it itself, and hooks/lib-common.sh's hook_path_slug (the same class minus '.' and '/') is that narrowing. The two boundaries differ on purpose and the difference is the whole claim: the CLI REJECTS a value that is not a slug, while the hooks SANITIZE first (hook_slug maps every other character to '-') so that a span is recorded rather than lost. So a harness-supplied value's characters still transit, dash-joined -- 'SECRET=hunter2 x' lands as 'SECRET-hunter2-x'. What the guard buys is that no field but note can carry whitespace, a newline, a quote or a control character, so nothing written through one can break the line format, smuggle a second JSON object or span two lines, and every value is length-bounded. It bounds the SHAPE and the SIZE of what reaches disk; it does not classify the content. Every value, note included, is capped at max_value_length characters on append, and over-long is a reject rather than a truncation. An earlier version claimed there was no free-text field at all while run_id, capability_id and agent accepted one, which is the shape of claim this registry must not carry. Adding another free-text field is a compatibility event (docs/COMPATIBILITY.md), never a convenience. Written by the hooks in written_by through hooks/lib-common.sh's hook_span; the agent span is a PAIR, where announce-agent-dispatch.sh writes only the start marker (a PreToolUse and its PostToolUse are separate processes, so the start instant has to survive on disk) and announce-agent-return.sh writes the line, which is why both are listed. All of it runs under the same opt-in gates as the events: only where .engineos/ exists, only when ENGINEOS_TELEMETRY is not 0, never in a bypassed session. Those hooks see no model usage, so agent spans carry tokens_in/tokens_out 0 and no cost_micros at all; a 0 there means unknown, never free. tool and model spans, real token counts and real costs come from a headless runner that owns the model call and does not exist yet. Reaped by hooks/ensure-project-layout.sh on telemetry.retention_days -- the '*.jsonl' glob already covers <session>.exec.jsonl. Consumed by the breaker's consecutive-failure count (rules/parallelism.md 'Circuit breaker'), which needs a status source that actually observes failure: the dispatch hooks' status is a FLOOR on that count, since a structured tool_response with no error flag reads as OK. Mirrored in rules/observability.md 'Agent traces'; C27 checks the block, the running CLI and the prose together.

router.note: Escalation policy for the P3 router agent: when the deterministic kernel answer is not enough and a model must produce a dispatch plan. Read by scripts/kernel.sh route-escalate; the fixtures are asserted by validate-engineos.sh C18e and scripts/test-kernel.sh.

scoring.note: Tier 1 fallback classifier (src/kernel/score.ts). Placeholders: v1 registries route exactly as the any-match router did; T13 calibrates from the golden set. bm25_weight < min_score so exemplar similarity alone never routes until calibrated.

combination.note: Declared invariants of src/kernel/combine.ts, checked by C38c; the loader refuses any other value (fail closed).

source_markers.note: Literal prefixes (after leading whitespace) that mark text the user did not type, matched by src/hooks/prompt-source.ts as literals, never as regular expressions. Verified by T05 against captured payloads; T13 captures a real UserPromptSubmit payload to confirm no host prefixes a SYSTEM NOTIFICATION frame to text the user typed.

tiebreak.note: Embedding tie-break (rev 3, contracts §4.7). Read by src/kernel/combine.ts only on an ambiguous deterministic route with a tiebreak fact; the daemon is opt-in (ENGINEOS_EMBED_DAEMON=1). Placeholders until T13 calibrates against the golden set with the pinned MiniLM revision.

migrate all services to the new logging format across all packages
build the ios release and upload to TestFlight
why does the login handler fail with a 500

judge.note: TypeSafe Jev as the opt-in semantic judge (ADR docs/adr/2026-10-10-three-tier-router-and-jev-judge.md). Off unless the enabled_env equals enabled_value AND key_env is non-empty; key_env is the NAME of the environment variable holding the key, and no key material ever lives in this registry. Prompts leave the machine: redaction runs before the request; mode shadow records only. Every threshold is a placeholder until T13; intent_default and rule_default must be above 0, because a zero cut would make an intent or rule the judge never scored qualify.

redaction.note: Applied, in list order, to the prompt text before it enters the judge state and before it reaches the tie-break daemon; each match becomes <redacted:kind>, so an earlier, more specific kind (private-key-block, sk-ant-) wins over a later, broader one (private-key, sk-). Classes: private keys (PEM/PGP block end to end, and an unterminated header with its body), Google private_key_id, JWTs, prefixed provider tokens (Anthropic, OpenAI, sk-, Stripe sk_/rk_, AWS access key id, GitHub gho_/ghp_/ghr_/ghs_/ghu_/github_pat_, GitLab, npm, Hugging Face, Google, Atlassian, Slack), URL credentials (the password part may hold an at sign), HTTP basic-scheme and bearer credentials, an AWS secret access key in an assignment, generic password/secret/token/api key/credential assignments (bare or quoted values), and personal data (email, E.164 phone, Brazilian national phone, CNPJ and CPF). A superset of install.sh SECRET_PATTERNS, which keeps its own bash copy (no node at install time) and stays a secrets-only gate. The shipped set is linear; the loader refuses unbounded quantifiers (*, +, {m,}) and quantified groups holding alternation or nested quantifiers, and pins this exact list by SHA-256 in src/registry/policy-judge.ts, so changing, adding, removing or reordering a pattern is a reviewed code change. The caller also caps the text before redacting (judge: 2 x max_state_bytes chars, tie-break: 2 x its text limit) and cuts to the final limit afterwards. Each pattern is a JavaScript RegExp source, compiled with flag g by the loader only to refuse one that does not compile.
